clue.text: I can't be arsed about a meeting called by May?

definitions.note: Theresa May, as Prime Minister, summoned her senior ministers to sit together

indicators.note: slang 'arsed' (bothered, or messed about) tells us to jumble the letters of the words just before it

explanation.surface: Someone too idle to bother with a gathering the Prime Minister has summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arsed' looks like idle slang ('can't be arsed' = can't be bothered) but it is the anagram signal on I CAN'T BE; 'about' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Prime Minister's senior ministers meeting together form this body; Theresa May was PM when the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Price to pay having made love last in Mafia fling

indicators.note: the zero is made into another letter, swapping one for the other

parts.note: cost is the price to pay
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A mobster's affair, after sex, comes at a price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made love' and 'fling' suggest an affair; the O of COST is made into A, the end of Mafia.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw or hurl, which is what fling means.

clue.text: Budweiser Corporation?

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a big belly, and one produced by Budweiser comes from drinking

explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built up by heavy drinking of beer, such as the American lager named, is jokingly a corporation.

clue.text: Irritable, having to take off second crap keeper?

indicators.note: removing a letter from the front

parts.note: snappy means short-tempered

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper made tetchy by being substituted after a second poor save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crap keeper' suggests a poor goalkeeper, but a baby's waste is kept in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's absorbent pants hold its faeces; this is the British word for a diaper.

clue.text: Very sad short story about revolutionary Cuban?

indicators.note: around, so the cut story surrounds the other letters
short means missing the last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: turned around, revolving, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a Cuban is a cigar from Cuba

explanation.surface: A sad short story about a Cuban rebel, Che perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary Cuban' points to Castro or Guevara, but a Cuban is a cigar, turned round to RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An old form of 'tragic', describing something deeply distressing and sorrowful.

clue.text: Computer firm stumped over web-based programs

parts.note: Apple is the computer maker

indicators.note: in cricket an over ends a set of balls, here read as 'turned over', so the letters go backwards

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A tech company is baffled by some internet software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' reads as baffled but gives the cricket abbreviation ST, which 'over' turns round to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small programs that run inside a web browser are given this diminutive name for little applications.

clue.text: Short lad getting in brews for boozers

indicators.note: the short lad gets inside the brews

parts.note: ales are brews

indicators.note: short means missing the last letter

parts.note: a kid is a lad

explanation.surface: A small boy lays in some beers for heavy drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for alcoholics, people who drink to excess.

clue.text: Rugby player worried around a German breed

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces goes around the next two

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A rugby forward fretting about a German rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives ATE as in 'what's eating you?'; 'around' means the rugby player and the worry together wrap round the German pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed animals or plants is to reproduce and multiply them.

clue.text: It goes up with the start of my self-love

indicators.note: up as in stirred up, so the letters are mixed
the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Vanity rises when the speaker thinks about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like rising but is the anagram signal on IT GOES; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive conceit and preoccupation with oneself is vanity, a love of self.

clue.text: News Romney spread about Clinton for Trump?

indicators.note: spread out, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Mitt Romney spreads stories about Hillary Clinton on Trump's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' reads as spreading news but signals the anagram of NEWS ROMNEY; 'about' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillary Clinton was Donald Trump's bitter rival in the 2016 election, an implacable foe.

clue.text: We'll speak about a ramble when we're out!

indicators.note: 'about' here means scattered around, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone promises to discuss a country walk once they have gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' plays on being asleep (out for the count) rather than out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking about while unconscious in sleep is a wander taken when we are dead to the world.

clue.text: African people returning from Oron banks

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read backwards, from right to left
the words 'from Oron' bank, or hold in store, the letters we need inside them

explanation.surface: Members of a tribe going back home from the shores of Oron.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'from Oron' backwards (NOROMORF) and the people sit inside it; 'banks' looks like riverbanks but says the letters are held there.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest ethnic group of Ethiopia, also living in northern Kenya.

clue.text: Its success might see happy queen opening drink

definitions.text: Its success might see happy queen opening drink

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy and carefree

indicators.note: the queen is opening up the drink, sitting inside it

parts.note: a libation is a drink, especially one poured as an offering
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A cheerful gay man celebrates by uncorking a drink when the cause wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' is both the ER of the wordplay and slang for a gay man, so the whole clue pictures the movement's success being toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign for gay rights would, on success, leave homosexual people free and happy to celebrate.

clue.text: Reorder off braille menu

indicators.note: change the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A request to stop printing the restaurant's menu in braille.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for a list of dishes available in a restaurant.

clue.text: Ready for release on a restroom break?

definitions.meaning: a finished film is stored in reels, completed and awaiting its premiere
'can' is slang for a toilet, so someone there is in it

explanation.surface: A film finished and awaiting release, or a person who has popped out to the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Film-makers say a completed shoot is stored away in its tin; American slang calls the toilet the can.

clue.text: Gentle church song in which some take comfort?

parts.note: easy means gentle
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A soft hymn that brings some people solace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take comfort' sounds like finding solace in a hymn, but it means sitting comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, upholstered armchair is a seat that people sink into for comfort.

clue.text: Chaps in pursuit of half-cut bandit?

definitions.text: Chaps in pursuit of half-cut bandit?

indicators.note: following behind, so the chaps come after
half of the word is cut away, losing its first three letters

parts.note: an outlaw is a bandit
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fellows chasing a drunken robber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as British slang for drunk but signals losing half of the bandit's word; sheriffs really do chase bandits, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheriffs and marshals of the Wild West were the officers of justice who hunted down bandits.

clue.text: Very unstable conical explosive

indicators.note: unstable letters are not fixed and can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cone-shaped bomb that is dangerously unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' looks like a noun for the bomb, but it is the adjective defined; 'unstable' rearranges CONICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperament or situation that may erupt violently is like a mountain about to blow.

clue.text: Bug company from the East in desire for IT?

indicators.note: the reversed company sits in the middle of the desire

parts.note: IT is sex appeal, so craving it is lust

indicators.note: read from the East means from right to left, in reverse

explanation.surface: A computer glitch in a firm out East, or someone keen on information technology.
explanation.walkthrough: IT suggests computing, as does 'Bug', but here IT is sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper-like insect that swarms; 'bug' is loosely used for any insect.

clue.text: Companion with unopened lager and winning smile!

parts.note: CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: with the first letter removed

parts.note: lager is beer
up means ahead, as in a game

explanation.surface: A friend with a full can of lager, grinning after a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened lager' looks like a sealed can, but it means the first letter is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are encouraging commands to someone glum, urging them to brighten up.

clue.text: Import unlimited spirits? It might keep one going awhile!

definitions.text: It might keep one going awhile!

parts.note: import means importance, as does moment (a matter of moment)

indicators.note: without its limits, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: rums are spirits

explanation.surface: Bringing in duty-free spirits, the kind of drink that keeps a person going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' reads as a verb about bringing goods in, but here it is the noun meaning significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics' quantity of motion: a moving body carries on moving because of it.

clue.text: Can English dressing cock up pâté dish?

indicators.note: the first letters clothe the mistake, surrounding it

parts.note: a tin is a can
err means to blunder, British slang 'cock up'

explanation.surface: A tin of English salad dressing ruins a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' reads as salad dressing; it puts TINE around ERR. 'Cock up' is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthenware dish in which pâté is cooked, and by extension the pâté itself.

clue.text: Complaint from union about individual on drugs

indicators.note: the complaint goes around the individual

parts.note: a sexually transmitted disease, STD, is a complaint caught from sexual union
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A trade union grumbles about a single member who is taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavily under the influence of cannabis or similar drugs, in slang.

clue.text: Johnny Foreigner's language learner takes to heart?

parts.note: French is a foreign tongue

indicators.note: the learner is taken into the heart, placed inside it

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A stereotyped foreigner's tongue that a student warms to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny Foreigner' is a jokey British name for any foreigner, but 'Johnny' alone is British slang for a condom and is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber johnny is a condom, and a ribbed or knobbly one is called by this name.

clue.text: One cruising eatery wanting liberal for date

indicators.note: here the eatery wants, or is lacking, its date
one letter stands in for another

parts.note: a diner is an eatery

explanation.surface: A man cruising for a date in a restaurant would like a liberal partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruising' suggests looking for a date, but it is a ship on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going passenger ship, especially one on a cruise, is this kind of vessel.

clue.text: Music producer one deceives on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast, heard rather than seen, so the word sounds like

parts.note: a liar is one who deceives

explanation.surface: A record producer who lies to people on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests someone in the record industry, but an instrument makes music.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harp of ancient Greece is an instrument that produces music.

clue.text: Men in a docked brown vessel

indicators.note: the men go inside the other letters
docked means its tail is cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Sailors aboard a brown ship tied up in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' and 'vessel' paint a ship in harbour, but 'vessel' is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery carrying blood from the heart is the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Nobody messes with Tony around ten in Barking

indicators.note: messing with something muddles it, so these letters are jumbled
barking means mad, another sign of disorder; it is also a district of London

explanation.surface: No one interferes with Tony, who hangs around at ten in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the East London place but is slang for mad, backing up 'messes with' as the anagram signal on TONY + TEN IN; 'around' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An insignificant person, of no importance, is a nobody.

clue.text: Old detective flushed and out of breath?

parts.note: ex means former
PI is a private investigator
red in the face

explanation.surface: A former investigator, red-faced and panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of breath' is read literally: dead people have run out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Having died is having no breath left; the word also means breathed out.

clue.text: Support snorting grams on my funeral procession

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means after, so these letters follow

parts.note: 'Cor!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: the support takes the grams in as if sniffing them up

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
G is the abbreviation for grams

explanation.surface: A backer taking cocaine at a funeral, to general shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grams' and 'snorting' suggest drugs, but G simply goes inside TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of mourners and cars that follows the hearse is this formal procession.
